summary: SplitSync iteration 3 backend testing complete. All 62 pytest cases pass in serial mode (21 iteration-1 + 24 iteration-2 + 17 new iteration-3 cases). Verified new features: (1) Weighted shares split - POST /api/expenses with shares [{self:60},{alice:40}] amount=100 -> alice owes 40; amount=200 with shares [{self:1},{alice:2},{bob:1}] -> alice owes 100 and bob owes 50; is_split=true and split_with correctly derived from shares; (2) Backward compat - split_with without shares still yields equal split (200/3 each); (3) Shares with all values <=0 are sanitized to None (is_split=false, no balance impact); (4) POST /api/auth/currency now accepts USD/INR/EUR/GBP/JPY and rejects XYZ with 400; lowercase input is uppercased; (5) GET /api/fx returns positive float rates for all 5 currencies with USD=1.0, INR>1, JPY>1, updated_at present; (6) Regressions verified - settlement subtraction still works with shares-based balances (alice 40 - 15 = 25); recurring materialization still creates >=2 expenses for weekly EUR recurring starting 14 days ago; scan endpoint auth wiring intact.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 773 lines - past the 700-line threshold. Should be split into routers (auth, expenses, friends, groups, recurring, settlements, fx, scan), models, and services modules.

get_balances() re-fetches shares/split_with expenses and awaits convert_amount() per participant. For shares-based expenses, each share converts independently even though they share currency. Could aggregate rates once at handler start and do in-memory math.
In create_expense (server.py:459), `split_with = [pid for pid in friend_ids]` is `list(friend_ids)` - minor style, non-deterministic ordering since friend_ids is a set (order may differ per call).

shares sanitization silently drops all-zero/negative shares to None. If shares is provided but sanitized empty AND split_with was also empty, is_split becomes False - correct behavior but not documented; consider returning a validation error if caller explicitly sent shares but none were valid.
SUPPORTED_CURRENCIES is a module-level tuple hardcoded to (USD,INR,EUR,GBP,JPY). Duplicates the currency list used in _fetch_fx() fallback rates - consider single source of truth.

success_rate.backend: 100% (62/62 in serial; 56/62 under default -n 2 loadscope due to cross-worker fixture races - see context_for_next_testing_agent)

seed_data_creation: Same seed as prior iterations: user_test_fixture01 / test_token_abc / TEST_backend_tester@example.com via conftest fixture (now upsert-based). All test entities prefixed TEST_. Session-scoped cleanup on teardown.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iteration 3 fully validated. Run with `cd /app/backend && pytest tests/ -n 0 -v` for deterministic serial execution (all 62 pass). The default `pytest.ini` addopts `-n 2 --dist loadscope` causes cross-worker races on the shared seed user (expenses/currency/settlements mutated concurrently across test files) - 5-6 tests may flake in parallel mode. If a future iteration wants parallel test safety, either: (a) switch to `--dist loadfile`, (b) give each test file its own seed user, or (c) partition mutating tests into a single file. Feature endpoints themselves are race-free; only the tests are racy. Shares payload contract: List[Dict] with participant_id ('self'|friend_id) and share (positive weight, not %). Backend converts weights to fractions of total. All-<=0 shares silently become None. Home currencies now: USD, INR, EUR, GBP, JPY.
rca_of_issue: One test needed updating for the new feature: test_api.py::TestAuth::test_currency_update_invalid asserted EUR->400 (valid in iterations 1-2 when only USD/INR were supported). Iteration 3 expanded supported currencies to include EUR/GBP/JPY, so the test now sends 'XYZ' to verify the reject path. No product bugs found. Test infrastructure has a pre-existing xdist race (shared seed user across worker-parallelized test classes) that iteration 3 exacerbates because there are now 3 mutating test files instead of 2; workaround is `-n 0`.
